query: How do I start a compost heap at home?
answer:
Find a level spot that gets some shade and drains well, then either make a simple pile about 3 feet (1 m) across or use a bin. Start with a 4–6 inch layer of "browns" (dry leaves, twigs, straw, shredded cardboard) on the bottom. Then keep adding layers, roughly 2–3 parts browns to 1 part "greens" by volume. Greens are things like vegetable and fruit scraps, coffee grounds and fresh grass clippings [1][2][3]. A good way to keep the mix about right is to measure both with the same bucket [4]. Leave out meat, dairy, fats and pet waste, because they smell and draw pests [1][3].

Keep the pile about as damp as a wrung-out sponge, and turn it with a fork every week or two to let air in. If it dries out, it stops breaking down [1][3]. If it smells bad, it's usually too wet or not getting enough air, so turn it and mix in more browns [1]. When it's dark and crumbly and smells like earth, which takes anywhere from a couple of months to about a year depending on how often you turn it, it's ready to spread on your garden.
